memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And are you now turning away from the Lord? If you rebel against the Lord today, tomorrow he will be angry with the whole community of Israel. If the land you possess is defiled, come over to the Lord's land, where the Lord's tabernacle stands, and share the land with us. But do not rebel against the Lord or against us by building an altar for yourselves, other than the altar of the Lord our God." — Josh 22:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The delegation makes an extraordinary offer. If the eastern tribes feel their land is somehow unclean or far from God, the western tribes say: come and share our land, live near the tabernacle with us — only do not turn from the Lord. This is not just rebuke; it is a costly invitation. They were willing to give up part of their own inheritance to keep their brothers close to God.

That is love. Beneath their fear of judgment was a genuine longing to keep the family together in faithfulness. They would rather share their land than lose their brothers to sin.

Notice too their awareness that our choices affect one another. "If you rebel today, tomorrow he will be angry with the whole community." In God's family, we are bound together. One person's walk with God touches the whole. This is not superstition; it is the reality of belonging to one another as God's people.

The New Testament says it clearly: we are members of one body, and if one part suffers, every part suffers with it (1 Cor 12:26). We are not isolated individuals. Your faithfulness strengthens others; your wandering can wound them. Let this move you both to guard your own walk and to draw straying brothers and sisters back with the kind of costly love shown here.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you recognise how your walk with God affects those around you?
2. Would you make a costly sacrifice to keep a brother close to God?
3. How can you draw others back with love rather than only rebuke?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that we belong to one another in Your family. Help me to guard my own walk and to love others enough to draw them back to You. Amen.
